title: Add comprehensive testing to parse command
description:
Comprehensive E2E testing for parse command following Farley/Fowler principles:

DOGFOODING EXERCISE (End-to-End CLI Boundary Testing):
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
These tests are DOGFOODING EXERCISES - they test the system from OUTSIDE IN through the actual CLI boundary, not internal implementation details. This follows Dave Farley's functional core / imperative shell principle and Martin Fowler's end-to-end testing philosophy.

Testing Approach:
✓ Test through ACTUAL CLI: gleam run -- parse <file> --o=<output.cue>
✓ Test observable behavior: Exit codes, JSON output, error messages
✓ Test full workflows: Complete parsing workflow from input to output
✓ Don't test internals: Black-box testing, not white-box

EARS FORMAT TESTING:
- SHALL, WHEN/THEN, WHERE, SHALL NOT, IF/THEN patterns
- Mixed EARS patterns in single spec
- Nested EARS requirements
- Ambiguous EARS statements
- Invalid EARS syntax
Expected: Correct CUE spec generated, exit code 0

EDGE CASES:
- Empty requirements file
- Unicode/special characters in requirements
- Very long requirements (>1000 chars)
- Invalid --o flag (missing file)
- Duplicate behavior names
- CUE syntax errors in output
Expected: Appropriate error handling with exit codes 1-3

INTEGRATION TESTING:
- Parse → bead generation workflow
- Session creation from parse output
- Spec file loading and validation
- Error recovery and retry
- Cross-command state sharing
Expected: Clean integration, no orphaned state

END-TO-END TESTING:
- Full workflow: reqs.txt → parse → CUE spec → validate → lint
- Session management: Create, update, retrieve
- Error recovery paths: Missing files, invalid syntax, permission errors
- Round-trip: Requirements → CUE → back to requirements
Expected: Complete happy path, error recovery, state consistency

TEST COMMANDS:
- gleam run -- parse test_reqs.txt --o=out.cue && echo "Pass: happy path"
- gleam run -- parse empty.txt && echo "Pass: empty input"
- gleam run -- parse invalid.txt && echo "Pass: error handling"
- gleam run -- parse && echo "Pass: usage message"
- cue vet out.cue schema/spec.cue && echo "Pass: CUE valid"

VALIDATION:
- Exit codes: 0 (success), 1 (error), 3 (invalid), 4 (internal)
- JSON structure: success flag, action, command, data, next_actions, metadata
- CUE output: Valid spec, proper types, correct structure
- File operations: Created files, cleaned temp files

NOT unit tests of:
- Internal parser functions
- CUE generation logic
- File I/O operations
